strings.name: Winnie Byanyima
strings.summary: Byanyima moved from aeronautical engineering into Ugandan politics, diplomacy and gender equality, later leading Oxfam and, from 2019, UNAIDS. She advocates access to medicines, women’s rights and economic fairness through community-centred HIV responses. In 2026 she announced departure at year-end and was appointed to chair IIED’s board from January 2027.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; reviewed on 15 November. This is not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Has led Oxfam and UNAIDS, long advancing public health, women’s rights and global economic fairness.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Bachelor’s in aeronautical engineering, University of Manchester; master’s in mechanical engineering, Cranfield University.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Health and medicine access
strings.highlights.h1.text: Leads UNAIDS and helped establish the People’s Medicines Alliance, advocating less discrimination and equitable access to health technologies.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Development and equality
strings.highlights.h2.text: Former Ugandan parliamentarian, diplomat and Oxfam leader, advancing women’s rights and global economic fairness.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Next appointment announced
strings.timeline.t1.text: UNAIDS announced her IIED board-chair appointment from January 2027; her UNAIDS mandate ends on 31 December 2026.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Began leading UNAIDS
strings.timeline.t2.text: Took up duties following her August appointment, with UN under-secretary-general rank.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Began leading Oxfam
strings.timeline.t3.text: Became Oxfam International executive director, serving until 2019.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Led UNDP gender team
strings.timeline.t4.text: Joined UNDP’s development-policy work to advance gender equality.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Led AU gender directorate
strings.timeline.t5.text: Became director of the AU’s Women, Gender and Development directorate.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Entered parliamentary and constitutional work
strings.timeline.t6.text: Participated in Uganda’s constitution-making and parliament, serving until 2004.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Became ambassador to France
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joined armed rebellion
strings.timeline.t8.text: Left engineering work and participated in the 1981–1986 armed rebellion.
